terra.problem: The passage does not say the angel had wings.
The passage says Jesus Christ sent His angel, not that God sent His angel.
Identifying Elijah as a prophet of Israel is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The passage says Jesus Christ sent His angel, not that God sent His angel.
Identifying Paul as an apostle is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The warning about nodding along and walking away sounds preachy rather than fatherly.
Papa Dorin can hold a writing instrument with his mustache; he used a pencil to write his note in the drawer.
Gabriel bringing messages to people is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Identifying Moses as Israel's leader is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The title about the kings comes after the title about the firstborn from the dead, not before it.
Papa Dorin guesses that he will be part of the Bible event when Jesus comes. He never puts himself in a Bible event.
The passage does not say the event will be loud. Mourning does not necessarily establish its volume.
Saying temple builders are in the Bible refers to a Bible fact outside the passage without a reference.
Calling Cyprus an island in the Bible is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Calling Crete an island in Scripture is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The cookie-cutter comparison does not fit the point about identifying an island. The shapes have nothing to do with John's location.
Saying John is told to write it down so it can travel adds a reason the text does not give.
Calling the roar real turns the text's comparison into a literal roar. His voice was like the roar of many waters.
The text does not say the point of the comparison is that the face was hard to look at. Papa Dorin cannot add a reason for John's choice of words, even as a guess.
Saying John is not left on the floor implies he gets up or is lifted. The passage says a hand is placed on him, but does not say he rises.
John already heard an instruction to write before he turned and saw the One like the Son of Man.
These are not the first words John hears from the voice. He hears the instruction to write before he turns.
The voice has already spoken to John before he falls, so these are not its first words.
The joke compares Papa Dorin's keys with the Living One's keys of Death and Hades, making a sacred claim the subject of the joke.
Calling the command one about this vision narrows it beyond the text, which also names the things that are and the things that will happen after this.
Saying the phrase appears elsewhere in the Bible refers to Scripture outside the passage without a reference.
